text:
Never felt closer to a fundamental change in how we build retrievers, and a different kind of memory for agents.

ARI is basically test-time training for retrievers, where gradients derived from a reasoning model's preferences teach the retriever where to look *at search time*.

Lots more to do here to get oblique search queries as manageable as non-oblique ones, and that will include first figuring out sub-linear (late-interaction-esque) search.

But the path ahead has never been clearer. Read @dianetc_'s blog!

So proud and grateful to have this support from @gabepereyra @nikogrupen and team at @harvey - long been a fan of their open sharing of contributions in this space like LAB and extremely early ventures into post-training RLMs!

As the capability of weight space programming begins to take shape and evals for it pop up (stay tuned!), I believe it will carry the highest odds at changing our notions of optimization and learning the most, and perhaps resolving the bottlenecks of deep learning that we simply accepted so far, like terrible sample efficiency.

A ton of work to be done here - watch for it from @rikiyatakehi and @jayden_teoh_ in the coming weeks.
